title: Functional compatibility as a determinant of persistent neural learning
abstract: arXiv:2608.22462v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Artificial neural networks can acquire new capabilities but often damage existing ones when they continue to learn. This stability-plasticity problem has motivated replay, regularization and constrained-update methods, yet it remains unclear whether a property of incoming learning itself determines what can be retained without disrupting protected behaviour. Here we show that functional compatibility, the extent to which new learning can coexist with behaviour that must be preserved, is a causal determinant of persistent learning. To our knowledge, this is the first controlled causal demonstration in which compatibility is deliberately changed from matched neural states and persistent learning is measured under a common retention requirement. translated_title: 功能兼容性作为持久神经学习的一个决定因素
translated_abstract: 人工神经网络可以获取新能力，但在继续学习时往往会损害已有能力。这一稳定性-可塑性问题促使了重放、正则化和约束更新等方法的发展，但尚不清楚新学习本身的一个属性是否决定了在不干扰受保护行为的情况下能保留什么。在这里，我们展示了功能兼容性——新学习与必须保留的行为共存的程度——是持久学习的一个因果决定因素。据我们所知，这是首次受控因果演示，其中兼容性被有意地从匹配的神经状态中改变，并在共同的保留要求下测量持久学习。该效应在独立学习方向、卷积和变压器架构、视觉和文本以及额外随机种子中普遍存在。学习规则在如何高效地利用这种兼容性方面有所不同。
tldr: 功能兼容性，即新学习与需保留行为共存的度量，被首次证明是持久神经学习的因果决定因素，并在多种架构和任务中普遍适用。
en_tdlr: Functional compatibility, the degree to which new learning coexists with preserved behavior, is causally shown for the first time to determine persistent neural learning, generalizing across architectures and tasks.
